messages:
Morgan: Quick thought — can we try a tiny, opinionated postmortem follow-up template? goal: cut open remediations and make IC handoffs predictable. sketch below, open to bikeshedding.

Alex: Love this. Narrow templates + automation = less context-switch. Can we tie to a single source of truth (github issue or Notion) so reporters + owners see status? :+1:

Priya: Agree. Also we should tag recurring patterns at the action-item level (e.g., `kv-cache`, `routing-fallback`, `auth-throttle`). helps triage and long-term trends.

Chris: Proposed lightweight template (1-sentence owner/ETA + one checkbox for recurrence check). minimal: 
```
- Owner: @alex
- Due: 2026-04-05
- What changed: increase batch size -> OOMs on M60
- Rollout plan: rollback batch-config on canary -> prod
- Post-checks: latency and OOM metric graphs
- Recurrence tag(s): kv-cache, memory-pressure
- Status: open / in-progress / done
```

Sam: +1. Suggest two small process rules: (1) every remediation must have an owner assigned before postmortem closure, (2) if owner is >72h unresponsive, escalation to oncall lead.

Taylor: For IC rotation: propose 2-week primary IC, 1-week secondary shadow. handoff doc template: `incident-summary`, `open-actions (w/owner+due)`, `current-mitigations`. makes followups smoother.

Morgan: Nice. For cadence, how about: owner check-ins at 3d, 7d, 14d, and 30d. oncall-bot will ping owners automatically and add a brief status to the incident thread. If still open at 30d, it moves to a recurring remediation board for prioritization.

oncall-bot: Automated reminder: `/remediate ping --owner @alex --ts 2790012345 --when 3d` will post a follow-up message in the thread. sample command: 
```
/remediate create --owner @alex --due 2026-04-05 --tags kv-cache,memory-pressure --notify 3d,7d,14d,30d
```

Alex: Can we make the bot also create a small GitHub issue if the remediation touches infra code? then link back in the thread. reduces manual duplication.

Priya: Yes please. Also add an optional `recurrence-review` field with checkboxes for 30/90/180 days so we don't forget systemic issues.

Chris: I'll prototype a tiny script that converts the template into a GH issue and pings the oncall-bot. 30-min spike ETA tomorrow.

Sam: Process rule idea: "open-by-default, close-by-owner" — meaning we don't close incidents until all remediations are owned and a next-step is scheduled. prevents silent drift.

Taylor: +1 on rotation docs. Also recommend a monthly "remediation retro" where we surface actions older than 90 days with pattern tags. should live in ops meeting.

Morgan: Next steps I propose: 
1) Chris spike to generate GH issue from template (tomorrow)
2) Alex to draft oncall-bot commands and Notion/GH mapping (this week)
3) Priya to define pattern taxonomy (kv-cache, routing, auth, db, config) and a short onboarding doc (1 pager)
4) Taylor to add IC rotation + handoff template to runbook

Alex: I'll take (2). putting a short PR up for bot commands by Friday.

Priya: I'll sketch taxonomy and share examples.

Chris: Spike scheduled, will post results in this thread.

Sam: I can run the first remediation retro next month.

Morgan: Awesome. If nobody objects, I'll update the postmortem template in the runbook and add the automation checklist. thanks all. :tada:

Alex: :thumbsup:

Priya: LGTM

Chris: sounds good

oncall-bot: Reminder created: follow-ups will be posted at 3d/7d/14d/30d.
